newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Minatitlan refinery reopens after fire.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Minatitlan refinery reopens after fire.

text.p: Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), Mexico's oil and gas monopoly, said Thursday that its Minatitlan refinery in Veracruz state reopened after a one-day closure following a small fire at one of the complex's plants.
The company said the 32 plants within the refinery have a crude processing capacity of 200,000 barrels per day.
The plant reopened early Wednesday, the company said, after activity was suspended for about 24 hours following a small fire.
The fire was extinguished within 15 minutes, and the eight people injured from the fire were released after a brief hospital stay, Pemex said.
In 1994, the Minatitlan refinery accounted for 16.4 percent of Mexico's refining output.
Tuesday's fire follows an explosion at Pemex's natural gas Cactus complex in July and a three-day blaze at a gasoline storage facility outside Mexico City in October.
